rows.why: Item 1 asks how a stored value with different case or surrounding whitespace is read. Its pick trims and lowercases, so "Draft", " PUBLISHED " and "Merged" read as draft, published and merged, as the scenario expects.

Item 2 asks which old spellings map to a status. Its pick maps only 'in review', so 'under review', 'live' and the other aliases in the table would read as null. The scenario expects "under_review" to read as review and "LIVE" as published.

Item 3 asks what an unmatched value returns. Its pick returns null and never guesses the nearest status, which is what the scenario requires. Item 7 also covers empty and whitespace-only values (also null), but item 3 is the closer match to the scenario's main point.
No item fixes this outcome. Item 5 (does writing normalise or accept only exact values) is about writing, but an exact value like "review" is stored as "review" whichever way item 5 is answered.

Item 5 asks whether writing normalises its input or accepts only exact enum values. Its pick accepts only exact lowercase values and throws on 'Draft', ' draft' and 'in-review', so it refuses the scenario's examples and never accepts old spellings on write. Item 6 covers only the error message.

Item 8 asks how the batch read reports unreadable values. Its pick keeps every row (status null if unreadable) and lists each distinct raw value once, sorted. Item 9 confirms values are reported as stored, so the scenario's 'exactly as it was stored' holds too.
